title: Self-Lubricating Bushes in the Cargo Door Latch Shaft Bearings

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Grease-free bushes in the cargo door latch shaft bearings, adopted after latch stiffness reports traced to washed-out lubricant on aircraft operating in heavy rain and de-icing conditions.

sections.reason: Ground handling staff reported increasing effort to close the cargo door on aircraft based at wet-climate stations, and a small number of doors failed to reach the latched position without a second attempt. Investigation of eleven reports found the shaft bearing grease washed out or contaminated with de-icing fluid in every case. The greased bush needs a lubrication task every six hundred flight hours which line stations were completing late or not at all, so the design answer preferred was a bearing that does not need lubrication rather than a stricter task.
sections.description: The greased bronze bushes in the four latch shaft bearings of each cargo door are replaced by self-lubricating liner bushes. The latch stiffener D5230135108629 is machined to the new bore and the retaining angle D5230139019163 is replaced by an item with a deeper spigot so that the bush is captive without a staking operation. Blind rivets EN989730K5 and swaged collars LN181939-7B secure the retainer. The latch actuator, functional item number 331WT4, and the door warning sensor 8511WT are not changed, but the sensor target plate is re-shimmed because the shaft end float is reduced by 0.3 mm. Revised detail is on drawings D52301313433 and D52301387215. Work is done from inside the cargo compartment in zones 831 and 891 with the door in the maintenance position.
sections.effects: Mass change is negligible at 0.2 kg per aircraft. No electrical load change. The bushes are one-way interchangeable: a post-modification door may be fitted with the old bush at the price of reinstating the lubrication task, but a pre-modification bore cannot take the new item. The six-hundred-hour lubrication task is deleted for the latch shaft bearings only, and the door proximity sensing rigging check gains a shim measurement step. Illustrated parts content for the latching figure needs both standards listed.
sections.embodiment_note: Cut in on the production line at MSN C00321 in August 2020. Retrofit is available through Service Bulletin CRN-52-1015 and takes one night stop per door with the door in the maintenance position. Bushes are supplied as a matched set of four; single-bush replacement is not permitted.

type_data.production_impact: Cut-in at MSN C00321, no line stoppage
